# Active return (annualized, arithmetic) (`active_return`)

*Category: Benchmark-relative analysis · Nature: estimated · Unit: decimal_return · Formula id: `active_return@v1` · Methodology 0.1.0*

## 1. What does it measure?

Average fund-minus-benchmark return, annualized.

## 2. Formula

```text
P * mean(r_fund,t - r_bench,t)
```

## 3. Required inputs

Fund and benchmark returns on aligned periods with a regular frequency. A benchmark is required.

## 4. Is higher or lower better?

Higher is better.

## 5. Plain-language interpretation

How much the fund returned above (or below) the benchmark per year, on average.

## 6. Professional interpretation

Arithmetic active return, consistent with the Information Ratio numerator; differs from the difference of geometric annualized returns (the PerformanceAnalytics ActivePremium).

## 7. Assumptions

- Linear annualization of the mean.

## 8. When can it be misleading?

- The benchmark is not representative of the strategy's opportunity set.
- The overlap with the benchmark is short.

## 9. Minimum sensible data

At least 2 aligned observations; low confidence below 3 years of overlap. (policy `benchmark_simple`: Requires at least 2 aligned observations; low confidence below 3 years of overlap, moderate below 5 years.)

## 10. Reference implementations

| Library | Function | Agrees | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| PerformanceAnalytics 2.0.4 (R) | `ActivePremium` | no (documented difference) | Difference of geometric annualized returns. |

## 11. Sources

- Grinold, R. C., & Kahn, R. N. (2000). Active Portfolio Management (2nd ed.). McGraw-Hill.

## 12. OpenFactsheet convention

Arithmetic mean of active returns x periods per year (decision 0012).
